title: Garlic butter shrimp orzo
equipment: 12-inch deep skillet or wide pot with lid

items: 1 lb large shrimp (21–25 per lb), peeled and deveined, patted dry
2½ cups low-sodium chicken broth, plus more as needed
2 large handfuls baby spinach (about 2 oz), or ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley

steps: Toss the shrimp with the salt, pepper and paprika.
Melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the orzo and toast 2–3 min, stirring, until lightly golden. Add the garlic and stir 30 sec, until fragrant.

Pour in the broth and bring to a boil over high heat. Turn to medium-low and simmer uncovered about 8 min, stirring every minute or two so it doesn't stick, until the orzo is almost tender and most of the broth is absorbed.
If the pan looks dry, add ¼ cup broth. Nestle the shrimp into the orzo in one layer, cover and cook 3–4 min, until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the lemon zest, lemon juice, parmesan and spinach until the spinach wilts and the orzo is creamy. Season with salt and pepper.
tips: Thaw frozen shrimp overnight in the fridge, or in a bowl of cold water for 10–15 min.
Shrimp are done when they curl into a loose C. A tight O means they're overcooked.
Orzo keeps soaking up liquid. Stir in a splash of broth right before serving if it gets thick.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet over low heat with a splash of broth, or in the microwave at 50% power, stirring. Doesn't freeze well; the shrimp turn rubbery.
